_[Consequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consequence_\(publication\) "Consequence (publication)")_ thought the song recalled pop rock music featured in the television series _[Glee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glee_\(TV_series\) "Glee (TV series)")_ (2009–2015) and the film _[Freaky Friday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freaky_Friday_\(2003_film\) "Freaky Friday (2003 film)")_ (2003).[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Ragusa-32)

In "Bad Idea Right?", Rodrigo contemplates whether it is a good idea to reconnect with her ex-boyfriend by weighing the pros and cons.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-PeopleVideo-33)[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Consequence-63) Narrated as an [inner monologue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrapersonal_communication "Intrapersonal communication"),[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-PeopleVideo-33) some of the song's lyrics depict her trying to convince herself not to do it while others see her justifying the encounter.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-BBpodcast-50)[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-ElleLyrics-64) In the first verse,[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-VarietyVideo-44) Rodrigo describes being out and intoxicated while receiving a phone call from the ex in real-time, perceiving hidden meanings in what he is saying.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-RSVideo-42)[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-PitchforkBNT-61) While she briefly feels that she should "probably not" reconnect with him, Rodrigo dismisses this thought.[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Pitchfork-65) Rodrigo repeatedly questions whether it is "a bad idea, right?" in the pre-chorus but concludes that it is fine.[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-ElleLyrics-64)[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-TLOBF-66) She tries to justify the decision to her friends, stating that she only considers him a friend but admitting that is "the biggest lie I ever said".[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Pitchfork-65)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-NMEvideo-10) Rodrigo also tries to pretend that she innocently slipped and fell on the ex's bed.[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Pitchfork-65)[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-MusicOMH-67) She recalls telling her friends that she was sleeping, but neglecting to mention that she was at another person's apartment.[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Petridis-68) _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")_'s Cat Zhang interpreted the song as Rodrigo's thoughts while under the influence of alcohol and believed that the ex might have been less attractive than Rodrigo describes him as in the song.[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-ElleLyrics-64)[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Pitchfork-65)

"Bad Idea Right?" received positive reviews from music critics. On August 11, 2023, _Pitchfork_ named the song as the "Best New Track".[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-PitchforkBNT-61) Zoladz described "Bad Idea Right?" as one of Rodrigo's "spunkiest, funniest and most irresistible singles yet".[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-NYTimesBestOf-69) _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s Jason Lipshutz ranked the song as the fifth-best track on _Guts_ and believed it sounded fresher with repeated listens as he better understood the gradations of her vocal performance.[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Lipshutz-70) [Sputnikmusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sputnikmusic "Sputnikmusic")'s Sowing thought it was more effective in the context of _Guts_ than upon its release as a single.[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Sputnikmusic-71) Alex Berry of _[Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash_\(magazine\) "Clash (magazine)")_ enjoyed how it contrasted the ballads on _Guts_ and believed it proved Rodrigo's versatility, establishing her distinctive style.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Clash-27)

Critics described "Bad Idea Right?" as a departure from the serious and balladic nature of "Vampire".[\[c\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-73) Punch Liwanag of the _[Manila Bulletin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_Bulletin "Manila Bulletin")_ praised the energetic and up-tempo production of "Bad Idea Right?" as a welcome change from the piano-driven ballads that had famed Rodrigo.[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-ManilaBulletin-74) Reviewers thought the song was youthful like her previous music but lyrically reflected themes more oriented to college than high school.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-BPM-30)[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-AVClubvideo-52) Some believed its lyrics were funny[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-MusicOMH-67)[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-MikaelWood-75)[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-NYTimesBestOf-69) and successfully made the idea of Rodrigo reconnecting with her ex sound appealing.[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-GuardianBestOf-56)[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Pitchfork-65)[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Treble-76) Writing for _[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_\(website\) "Vulture (website)")_, Craig Jenkins thought "Bad Idea Right?" signified Rodrigo's ability to create songs deeply grounded in her personal experiences that still resonate universally.[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Vulture-62) Lines from the song were included on _[GQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GQ "GQ")_'s list of the album's standout and "gutsiest" lyrics and _[Nylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nylon_\(magazine\) "Nylon (magazine)")_'s list of its impeccable lyrics.[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Nylon-77)[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-78)

Others praised Rodrigo's performance on "Bad Idea Right?". _Pitchfork_'s Shaad D'Souza called it one of the year's standout pop performances and Rodrigo a great performer; he noted that her strong commitment to playing a character made the song succeed, which was echoed by the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_'s Mikael Wood.[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-PitchforkBNT-61)[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-LATimesAbrams-35) _[The Line of Best Fit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Line_of_Best_Fit "The Line of Best Fit")_'s Matthew Kim thought her impassive delivery of the line "fuck it, it's fine" amplified and complemented the album's diverse spectrum of emotions, while Zoladz thought it was done with precise comedic timing.[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-TLOBF-66)[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-NYT8More-41) Mark Richardson of _[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")_ and Wood believed "Bad Idea Right?" benefited from her background as an actress, with the latter stating it displayed "pitch-perfect line readings that shift between comic registers on a dime — from naturalistic to screwball, faux-earnest to [deadpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpan "Deadpan")".[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-MikaelWood-75)[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-WSJ-55)

In September 2023, Jessie Atkinson of _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ listed "Bad Idea Right?" as Rodrigo's sixth-best song and [Rob Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Sheffield "Rob Sheffield") of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ ranked it seventh in her discography. cons.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-PeopleVideo-33)[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Consequence-63) Narrated as an [inner monologue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrapersonal_communication "Intrapersonal communication"),[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-PeopleVideo-33) some of the song's lyrics depict her trying to convince herself not to do it while others see her justifying the encounter.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-BBpodcast-50)[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-ElleLyrics-64) In the first verse,[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-VarietyVideo-44) Rodrigo describes being out and intoxicated while receiving a phone call from the ex in real-time, perceiving hidden meanings in what he is saying.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-RSVideo-42)[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-PitchforkBNT-61) While she briefly feels that she should "probably not" reconnect with him, Rodrigo dismisses this thought.[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Pitchfork-65) Rodrigo repeatedly questions whether it is "a bad idea, right?" in the pre-chorus but concludes that it is fine.[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-ElleLyrics-64)[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-TLOBF-66) She tries to justify the decision to her friends, stating that she only considers him a friend but admitting that is "the biggest lie I ever said".[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Pitchfork-65)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-NMEvideo-10) Rodrigo also tries to pretend that she innocently slipped and fell on the ex's bed.[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Pitchfork-65)[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-MusicOMH-67) She recalls telling her friends that she was sleeping, but neglecting to mention that she was at another person's apartment.[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Petridis-68) _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")_'s Cat Zhang interpreted the song as Rodrigo's thoughts while under the influence of alcohol and believed that the ex might have been less attractive than Rodrigo describes him as in the song.[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-ElleLyrics-64)[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Pitchfork-65)

"Bad Idea Right?" received positive reviews from music critics. On August 11, 2023, _Pitchfork_ named the song as the "Best New Track".[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-PitchforkBNT-61) Zoladz described "Bad Idea Right?" as one of Rodrigo's "spunkiest, funniest and most irresistible singles yet".[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-NYTimesBestOf-69) _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s Jason Lipshutz ranked the song as the fifth-best track on _Guts_ and believed it sounded fresher with repeated listens as he better understood the gradations of her vocal performance.[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Lipshutz-70) [Sputnikmusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sputnikmusic "Sputnikmusic")'s Sowing thought it was more effective in the context of _Guts_ than upon its release as a single.[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Sputnikmusic-71) Alex Berry of _[Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash_\(magazine\) "Clash (magazine)")_ enjoyed how it contrasted the ballads on _Guts_ and believed it proved Rodrigo's versatility, establishing her distinctive style.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Clash-27)

Critics described "Bad Idea Right?" as a departure from the serious and balladic nature of "Vampire".[\[c\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-73) Punch Liwanag of the _[Manila Bulletin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_Bulletin "Manila Bulletin")_ praised the energetic and up-tempo production of "Bad Idea Right?" as a welcome change from the piano-driven ballads that had famed Rodrigo.[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-ManilaBulletin-74) Reviewers thought the song was youthful like her previous music but lyrically reflected themes more oriented to college than high school.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-BPM-30)[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-AVClubvideo-52) Some believed its lyrics were funny[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-MusicOMH-67)[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-MikaelWood-75)[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-NYTimesBestOf-69) and successfully made the idea of Rodrigo reconnecting with her ex sound appealing.[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-GuardianBestOf-56)[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Pitchfork-65)[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Treble-76) Writing for _[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_\(website\) "Vulture (website)")_, Craig Jenkins thought "Bad Idea Right?" signified Rodrigo's ability to create songs deeply grounded in her personal experiences that still resonate universally.[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Vulture-62) Lines from the song were included on _[GQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GQ "GQ")_'s list of the album's standout and "gutsiest" lyrics and _[Nylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nylon_\(magazine\) "Nylon (magazine)")_'s list of its impeccable lyrics.[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-Nylon-77)[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-78)

Others praised Rodrigo's performance on "Bad Idea Right?". _Pitchfork_'s Shaad D'Souza called it one of the year's standout pop performances and Rodrigo a great performer; he noted that her strong commitment to playing a character made the song succeed, which was echoed by the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_'s Mikael Wood.[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-PitchforkBNT-61)[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-LATimesAbrams-35) _[The Line of Best Fit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Line_of_Best_Fit "The Line of Best Fit")_'s Matthew Kim thought her impassive delivery of the line "fuck it, it's fine" amplified and complemented the album's diverse spectrum of emotions, while Zoladz thought it was done with precise comedic timing.[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-TLOBF-66)[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-NYT8More-41) Mark Richardson of _[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")_ and Wood believed "Bad Idea Right?" benefited from her background as an actress, with the latter stating it displayed "pitch-perfect line readings that shift between comic registers on a dime — from naturalistic to screwball, faux-earnest to [deadpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpan "Deadpan")".[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-MikaelWood-75)[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F#cite_note-WSJ-55)

In September 2023, Jessie Atkinson of _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ listed "Bad Idea Right?" as Rodrigo's sixth-best song and [Rob Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Sheffield "Rob Sheffield") of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ ranked it seventh in her discography. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Olivia_Rodrigo_signature.svg/250px-Olivia_Rodrigo_signature.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olivia_Rodrigo_signature.svg)

**Olivia Isabel Rodrigo** (born February 20, 2003) is an American singer-songwriter and actress. She began her career as a child actress, appearing in commercials and the [direct-to-video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct-to-video "Direct-to-video") film _[An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An_American_Girl:_Grace_Stirs_Up_Success "An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success")_ (2015). She rose to prominence with her leading roles in the [Disney Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Channel "Disney Channel") series _[Bizaardvark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bizaardvark "Bizaardvark")_ (2016–2019) and the [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") series _[High School Musical: The Musical: The Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_School_Musical:_The_Musical:_The_Series "High School Musical: The Musical: The Series")_ (2019–2022).

Rodrigo shifted her focus to music and signed with [Geffen Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geffen_Records "Geffen Records") in 2020. Her debut studio album, _[Sour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sour_\(album\) "Sour (album)")_ (2021), topped the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") and nine other charts worldwide. It was preceded by the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") number-one singles "[Drivers License](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drivers_License_\(song\) "Drivers License (song)")" and "[Good 4 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_4_U "Good 4 U")". She was the subject of a documentary, _[Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Rodrigo:_Driving_Home_2_U "Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U")_ (2022). Her next two studio albums, _[Guts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guts_\(album\) "Guts (album)")_ (2023) and _[You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Seem_Pretty_Sad_for_a_Girl_So_in_Love "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love")_ (2026), produced the US number-one singles "[Vampire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vampire_\(Olivia_Rodrigo_song\) "Vampire (Olivia Rodrigo song)")" and "[Drop Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drop_Dead "Drop Dead")" respectively, making her the first artist to have each lead single from their first three albums debut atop the chart.

[Rodrigo's accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Olivia_Rodrigo "List of awards and nominations received by Olivia Rodrigo") include three [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"), four [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards"), and seven [_Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Awards "Billboard Music Awards"). She was named _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time (magazine)")_'s [Entertainer of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Entertainer_of_the_Year "Time Entertainer of the Year") in 2021, _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s [Woman of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Woman_of_the_Year "Billboard Woman of the Year") in 2022, and [ASCAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCAP "ASCAP")'s Pop Music Songwriter of the Year in both 2022 and 2024.

## Early life

Olivia Isabel Rodrigo[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) was born on February 20, 2003,[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) at the [Rancho Springs Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancho_Springs_Medical_Center "Rancho Springs Medical Center") in [Murrieta, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murrieta,_California "Murrieta, California"), to Jennifer ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Née "Née") Lee), a schoolteacher, and Chris, a [family therapist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_therapist "Family therapist").[\[3\]](#cite_note-born_info_1-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) She is an only child,[\[5\]](#cite_note-snapes-heartbreak-5) and grew up in neighboring [Temecula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temecula "Temecula").[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) Rodrigo was born half-deaf in her left ear.[\[7\]](#cite_note-RS-7) She is half-Filipina and identifies as [Filipino American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipino_American "Filipino American").[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) Her paternal grandparents and great-grandparents emigrated from the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines"), and her family follows Filipino traditions, including preparation of [cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipino_cuisine "Filipino cuisine").[\[10\]](#cite_note-caam-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-BBC-5facts-11) Her mother has German and Irish ancestry.[\[5\]](#cite_note-snapes-heartbreak-5)[\[12\]](#cite_note-abscbn-12) She grew up listening to her parents' favorite [alternative rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_rock "Alternative rock") bands, such as [No Doubt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Doubt "No Doubt"), [Pearl Jam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Jam "Pearl Jam"), [the White Stripes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_White_Stripes "The White Stripes"), and [Green Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Day "Green Day").[\[13\]](#cite_note-variety-musicjourney-13)

Rodrigo attended Lisa J. Mails Elementary School in Murrieta, participating in its after-school musical theater program.[\[14\]](#cite_note-Murrieta2019-14) At age five, her parents signed her up for vocal lessons with Jennifer Dustman, who enrolled Rodrigo in various local singing competitions.[\[15\]](#cite_note-april2021-elle-profile-15) On Dustman's advice, Rodrigo's parents enrolled her in acting lessons.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Geena_Davis_bio-16)[\[17\]](#cite_note-allmusic-bio-17) She began taking piano lessons at age nine.[\[15\]](#cite_note-april2021-elle-profile-15) Rodrigo first became interested in songwriting after listening to [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") songs by [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"),[\[13\]](#cite_note-variety-musicjourney-13) and she was playing guitar by age 12.[\[17\]](#cite_note-allmusic-bio-17) In May 2010, at age seven, she first appeared onscreen in an [Old Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Navy "Old Navy") commercial.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

## Career

### 2015–2019: Career beginnings and acting

In 2015, at age twelve, Rodrigo made her acting debut, in the lead role of [Grace Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace_Thomas "Grace Thomas") in the direct-to-video film _[An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An_American_Girl:_Grace_Stirs_Up_Success "An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success")_.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) She attended Dorothy McElhinney Middle School in Murrieta for a year, then moved to Los Angeles after landing an acting role in [Disney Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Channel "Disney Channel")'s _[Bizaardvark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bizaardvark "Bizaardvark")_ in 2016;[\[14\]](#cite_note-Murrieta2019-14) she was homeschooled from then until graduating in 2021.[\[5\]](#cite_note-snapes-heartbreak-5)[\[21\]](#cite_note-21) Starring as the character Paige Olvera, a guitarist, she played the role for three seasons.[\[22\]](#cite_note-bizaardvark-22)[\[23\]](#cite_note-23)[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)

In February 2019, she was cast in the starring role of Nini Salazar-Roberts on the [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") series _[High School Musical: The Musical: The Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_School_Musical:_The_Musical:_The_Series "High School Musical: The Musical: The Series")_, which premiered in November of that year.[\[26\]](#cite_note-HSMTS-26) Rodrigo was praised for her performance,[\[27\]](#cite_note-27)[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) with Joel Keller of _[Decider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decider_\(website\) "Decider (website)")_ calling her "especially magnetic".[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) For the series, Rodrigo wrote and performed the promotional single "[All I Want](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_I_Want_\(Olivia_Rodrigo_song\) "All I Want (Olivia Rodrigo song)")", released in November 2019.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) She left the show at the end of its third season to focus on her music career.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

### 2020–2022: _Sour_

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Sour_Tour_2022.jpg/250px-Sour_Tour_2022.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sour_Tour_2022.jpg)

Rodrigo in 2022 during the Sour Tour

Rodrigo signed with [Geffen Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geffen_Records "Geffen Records") in 2020.[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) She negotiated the record deal to secure for herself ownership of the [masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastering_\(audio\) "Mastering (audio)") of her music.[\[5\]](#cite_note-snapes-heartbreak-5) On January 8, 2021, she released her debut single, "[Drivers License](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drivers_License_\(song\) "Drivers License (song)")", which she co-wrote with producer [Dan Nigro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Nigro "Dan Nigro").[\[34\]](#cite_note-34)[\[35\]](#cite_note-thelineofbestfit.com-35) Within the week of its release, "Drivers License" was critically acclaimed,[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) and broke [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify")'s record twice for most daily streams ever for a non-holiday song with over 15.7 million global streams on January 11 and over 17 million global streams the next day.[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) It went on to break another Spotify record for the first song in history to hit 80 million streams in seven days.[\[38\]](#cite_note-38) The song debuted at number one on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"),[\[39\]](#cite_note-DriversLicense_US_Number1-39) and reached number one in numerous other countries.[\[40\]](#cite_note-langford-DLstreaming-40)[\[41\]](#cite_note-shafer-DLstreaming-41) Rodrigo stated in an interview that "It's been the absolute craziest week of my life ... My entire life just, like, shifted in an instant."[\[42\]](#cite_note-42)

On April 1, 2021, Rodrigo released her follow-up single, "[Deja Vu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deja_Vu_\(Olivia_Rodrigo_song\) "Deja Vu (Olivia Rodrigo song)")", which debuted at number eight on the _Billboard_ Hot 100,[\[43\]](#cite_note-trust-2021-43) making her the first artist to debut their first two releases in the top 10 of the Hot 100.[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) The third single preceding her debut album, "[Good 4 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_4_U "Good 4 U")", followed on May 14, 2021, and became her second single to debut at number one on the Hot 100.[\[45\]](#cite_note-45)[\[46\]](#cite_note-46) _[Sour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sour_\(album\) "Sour (album)")_, her debut studio album, was released on May 21, 2021, to critical acclaim.[\[47\]](#cite_note-47) _[Slate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slate_\(magazine\) "Slate (magazine)")_'s Chris Molanphy said its first three singles alone established Rodrigo's "early status as [Gen-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gen-Z "Gen-Z")'s most versatile new artist".[\[48\]](#cite_note-molanphy-good4u-48) According to _[Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash_\(magazine\) "Clash (magazine)")_ critic Robin Murray, Rodrigo is regarded as one of Generation Z's finest artists,[\[49\]](#cite_note-49) while _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")_ dubbed her "the voice of her generation" in its cover story of Rodrigo.[\[13\]](#cite_note-variety-musicjourney-13) _Sour_ debuted at number one on the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") chart and spent a total of five weeks at the spot, becoming the longest reigning number-one album by a female artist in 2021.[\[50\]](#cite_note-50)

In June 2021, Rodrigo premiered _Sour Prom_, a [prom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prom "Prom")\-themed concert film on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[\[51\]](#cite_note-51) Three days later, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time (magazine)")_ named her Entertainer of the Year.[\[52\]](#cite_note-time-52) In an Instagram post on December 24, 2021, Rodrigo uploaded a snippet of a Christmas song called "The Bels" that she wrote and recorded at age five.[\[53\]](#cite_note-53)[\[54\]](#cite_note-54) According to _Billboard_, Rodrigo closed 2021 as the bestselling singles artist worldwide,[\[55\]](#cite_note-55) while placing eight songs on the year-end [Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") chart, including "Drivers License" at number four, "Good 4 U" at number nine, and "Deja Vu" at number 27.[\[56\]](#cite_note-56) In the US and UK, _Sour_ was respectively the third and fourth bestselling album of 2021.[\[57\]](#cite_note-forbes-bestselling-57)[\[58\]](#cite_note-OCC-bestselling-58) _Sour_ and "Drivers License" were also respectively Spotify's most-streamed album and song globally.[\[59\]](#cite_note-spotify2021-59) The [International Federation of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry") (IFPI) ranked Rodrigo as the tenth bestselling artist of 2021 and _Sour_ as the second bestselling album of 2021.[\[60\]](#cite_note-60)

To support _Sour_, Rodrigo embarked on her debut headlining tour, the [Sour Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sour_Tour "Sour Tour"), which ran from April to July 2022; it included stops in the United States, Canada, and Europe.[\[61\]](#cite_note-61) In February 2022, Rodrigo signed with [Lighthouse Management + Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse_Management_+_Media "Lighthouse Management + Media"), entering into a management arrangement with [Aleen Keshishian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleen_Keshishian "Aleen Keshishian") and Zack Morgenroth.[\[62\]](#cite_note-62) Rodrigo's Disney+ documentary film _[Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Rodrigo:_Driving_Home_2_U "Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U")_, which details the making of _Sour_, was released on March 25, 2022.[\[63\]](#cite_note-pitchfork-63) Rodrigo received seven nominations at the [64th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/64th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "64th Annual Grammy Awards"), including [Best New Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist"), [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") and [Best Pop Vocal Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Pop_Vocal_Album "Best Pop Vocal Album") for _Sour_, and [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year"), [Best Pop Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Pop_Solo_Performance "Best Pop Solo Performance") and [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year") for "Drivers License".[\[64\]](#cite_note-64) She won the awards for Best New Artist, Best Pop Vocal Album for _Sour_, and Best Pop Solo Performance for "Drivers License".[\[65\]](#cite_note-Grammys_2022-65) In 2022, while crafting her next album, _[Guts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guts_\(album\) "Guts (album)")_, Rodrigo attended a poetry class at [University of Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California "University of Southern California"), and ended up repurposing one of her homework pieces into the song "[Lacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacy_\(song\) "Lacy (song)")", which would appear on the album's tracklist.[\[66\]](#cite_note-66)

### 2023–2025: _Guts_

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Olivia_Rodrigo_%40_Theatre_at_Ace_Hotel_10_09_2023_%2853423846745%29.jpg/250px-Olivia_Rodrigo_%40_Theatre_at_Ace_Hotel_10_09_2023_%2853423846745%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olivia_Rodrigo_@_Theatre_at_Ace_Hotel_10_09_2023_\(53423846745\).jpg)

Rodrigo performing at the [Theatre at Ace Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatre_at_Ace_Hotel "Theatre at Ace Hotel") in 2023

On August 16, 2023, Rodrigo became the youngest artist to receive the [Brit Billion Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Billion_Award "Brit Billion Award") for achieving over one billion digital streams in the United Kingdom. She was the 19th artist to receive a BRIT Billion Award.[\[67\]](#cite_note-67) Rodrigo's second album, _Guts_, was released on September 8, 2023, and debuted atop the _Billboard_ 200. She stated that the album was about "growing pains" and self-discovery. Going into the album cycle, she felt that she had grown "10 years" between the ages of 18 and 20.[\[68\]](#cite_note-68) _Guts_ received critical acclaim from various outlets and was later declared by BBC News as the most critically acclaimed album of 2023.[\[69\]](#cite_note-69) The album's lead single, "[Vampire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vampire_\(Olivia_Rodrigo_song\) "Vampire (Olivia Rodrigo song)")", was released on June 30. It became Rodrigo's third single to [debut atop the _Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_number_ones_of_2023 "List of Billboard Hot 100 number ones of 2023"), making her the first artist ever to debut the lead singles from two career-opening albums at No. 1 on the Hot 100.[\[70\]](#cite_note-70)[\[71\]](#cite_note-71)[\[72\]](#cite_note-72) The album's second single, "[Bad Idea Right?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F "Bad Idea Right?")", was released on August 11, 2023,[\[73\]](#cite_note-73) and reached the top 10 in the US and UK.[\[74\]](#cite_note-74)[\[75\]](#cite_note-75)

On October 9, 2023, Rodrigo performed songs from _Guts_ in an exclusive concert in partnership with American Express at [Los Angeles Theater at Ace Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ace_Hotel_Los_Angeles "Ace Hotel Los Angeles"). All proceeds from ticket sales went to her Fund 4 Good nonprofit organization.[\[76\]](#cite_note-76) On October 18, 2023, Rodrigo announced that the four secret tracks released on limited vinyl editions of _Guts_ would be released as a limited vinyl-exclusive EP to commemorate [Record Store Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_Store_Day "Record Store Day") (RSD) Black Friday.[\[77\]](#cite_note-77) The EP _Guts: The Secret Tracks_ ranked as one of the top sellers during Record Store Day.[\[78\]](#cite_note-78) On November 3, Rodrigo released the song "[Can't Catch Me Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Catch_Me_Now "Can't Catch Me Now")" for _[The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hunger_Games:_The_Ballad_of_Songbirds_&_Snakes "The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes")_.[\[79\]](#cite_note-79) The song won the [Hollywood Music in Media Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Music_in_Media_Award "Hollywood Music in Media Award") for [Best Original Song in a Sci-Fi, Fantasy or Horror Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Music_in_Media_Award_for_Best_Original_Song_in_a_Sci-Fi,_Fantasy_or_Horror_Film "Hollywood Music in Media Award for Best Original Song in a Sci-Fi, Fantasy or Horror Film") at the [2023 ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/14th_Hollywood_Music_in_Media_Awards "14th Hollywood Music in Media Awards").[\[80\]](#cite_note-80)

To support _Guts_, Rodrigo embarked on her second headlining tour, the [Guts World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guts_World_Tour "Guts World Tour"), from February 2024 to July 2025, visiting North America, Europe, Asia, and Oceania.[\[81\]](#cite_note-81)[\[82\]](#cite_note-82) On March 22, 2024, Rodrigo released a deluxe version of _Guts_, titled _Guts (Spilled)_, with five additional songs, including the four secret tracks from the vinyl variants.[\[83\]](#cite_note-83) On April 13, 2024, Rodrigo made a special guest appearance at [No Doubt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Doubt "No Doubt")'s [Coachella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella "Coachella") show, where she performed the band's 2000 single "[Bathwater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bathwater_\(song\) "Bathwater (song)")" alongside them.[\[84\]](#cite_note-84) On October 2, 2024, Rodrigo announced the _[Guts World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guts_World_Tour "Guts World Tour")_ concert film, which was released on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") on October 29.[\[85\]](#cite_note-85)

Rodrigo performed at several music festivals in June 2025. On June 7, she headlined the second day of the [Governors Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Ball "Governors Ball"), where she performed a cover of "[Burning Down the House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Down_the_House "Burning Down the House")" with musician [David Byrne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Byrne "David Byrne"), founding member of [Talking Heads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talking_Heads "Talking Heads").[\[86\]](#cite_note-86)[\[87\]](#cite_note-87)[\[88\]](#cite_note-88) She was the headlining act for the 2025 BST Hyde Park Show on June 27, with support from [The Last Dinner Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_Dinner_Party "The Last Dinner Party") and [Girl in Red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girl_in_Red "Girl in Red").[\[89\]](#cite_note-89) Two days later, on June 29, she headlined the final day of the [2025 Glastonbury Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Glastonbury_Festival "2025 Glastonbury Festival") and performed on the [Pyramid Stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyramid_Stage "Pyramid Stage") in her largest performance in the UK to date. Her concert included a guest appearance by [Robert Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Smith_\(musician\) "Robert Smith (musician)"), with whom Rodrigo sang two songs by [the Cure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cure "The Cure"), "[Just like Heaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_like_Heaven_\(The_Cure_song\) "Just like Heaven (The Cure song)")" and "[Friday I'm in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friday_I'm_in_Love "Friday I'm in Love")".[\[90\]](#cite_note-90)[\[91\]](#cite_note-91) On August 1, she headlined the second day of [Lollapalooza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lollapalooza "Lollapalooza") Chicago 2025, with [Weezer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weezer "Weezer") guesting to perform the songs "[Buddy Holly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_Holly_\(song\) "Buddy Holly (song)")" and "[Say It Ain't So](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Say_It_Ain't_So "Say It Ain't So")" with her.[\[92\]](#cite_note-92) Rodrigo was featured in the documentary film _[Lilith Fair: Building a Mystery – The Untold Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lilith_Fair:_Building_a_Mystery "Lilith Fair: Building a Mystery")_ (2025), reflecting on the legacy of the all-female music festival.[\[93\]](#cite_note-93) On November 9, Rodrigo teamed up with [Feist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feist_\(singer\) "Feist (singer)") to perform a rendition of "[We're Going to Be Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We're_Going_to_Be_Friends "We're Going to Be Friends")" by [the White Stripes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_White_Stripes "The White Stripes") at the band's [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") induction ceremony.[\[94\]](#cite_note-94)

### 2026–present: _You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love_

On April 2, 2026, Rodrigo announced her third studio album, _[You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Seem_Pretty_Sad_for_a_Girl_So_in_Love "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love")_.[\[95\]](#cite_note-USAT-2026-95) Its lead single, "[Drop Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drop_Dead "Drop Dead")", was released on April 17[\[96\]](#cite_note-96) and debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, extending her record as the first artist to debut the lead singles from their first three albums at the summit.[\[97\]](#cite_note-97) "[The Cure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cure_\(Olivia_Rodrigo_song\) "The Cure (Olivia Rodrigo song)")" was released on May 22 as the album's second single,[\[98\]](#cite_note-98) followed by "[Stupid Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stupid_Song "Stupid Song")" as its third single alongside its release, accompanied by a music video.[\[99\]](#cite_note-99) Released on June 12, _You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love_ debuted at number one on the US _Billboard_ 200 and the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart"), marking Rodrigo's largest first-week sales in both countries.[\[100\]](#cite_note-yspsus-100)[\[101\]](#cite_note-yspsuk-101) Her third-consecutive US number-one album, it made her the first artist to have their first three lead singles and studio albums debut atop the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and _Billboard_ 200.[\[100\]](#cite_note-yspsus-100) In the UK, she became the youngest international artist to earn more than 100,000 opening-week units since [Britney Spears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_Spears "Britney Spears") in 2004.[\[101\]](#cite_note-yspsuk-101)

On April 18, Rodrigo appeared as a surprise guest on [Addison Rae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addison_Rae "Addison Rae")'s set at [Coachella 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_2026 "Coachella 2026") and debuted "Drop Dead" live.[\[102\]](#cite_note-102) On April 30, Rodrigo announced her third concert tour, [the Unraveled Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Unraveled_Tour "The Unraveled Tour"), in support of _You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love_. Consisting of 86 dates across North America and Europe, the tour will begin on September 25, 2026, in [Hartford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hartford "Hartford"), and conclude on May 10, 2027, in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"). Supporting acts include [Devon Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devon_Again "Devon Again"), [Die Spitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die_Spitz "Die Spitz"), [Grace Ives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace_Ives "Grace Ives"), [The Last Dinner Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_Dinner_Party "The Last Dinner Party") and [Wolf Alice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolf_Alice "Wolf Alice").[\[103\]](#cite_note-103)[\[104\]](#cite_note-104) Rodrigo appeared as both host and musical guest on _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")_ on May 2;[\[105\]](#cite_note-SNL2026-105) she performed "Drop Dead" and debuted another track, "[Begged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Begged_\(song\) "Begged (song)")".[\[106\]](#cite_note-106) During her surprise set at [Primavera Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primavera_Sound "Primavera Sound") on June 6, she debuted her new track, "[What's Wrong with Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What's_Wrong_with_Me "What's Wrong with Me")" with Robert Smith of the Cure.[\[107\]](#cite_note-107) On June 22, Rodrigo announced [Daisy Chain Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daisy_Chain_Fields "Daisy Chain Fields"), an all-female music festival set to take place on August 29 in [Irvine, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irvine,_California "Irvine, California"), with 16 other female artists set to perform and all net proceeds dire

Signature

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Olivia_Rodrigo_signature.svg/250px-Olivia_Rodrigo_signature.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olivia_Rodrigo_signature.svg)

**Olivia Isabel Rodrigo** (born February 20, 2003) is an American singer-songwriter and actress. She began her career as a child actress, appearing in commercials and the [direct-to-video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct-to-video "Direct-to-video") film _[An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An_American_Girl:_Grace_Stirs_Up_Success "An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success")_ (2015). She rose to prominence with her leading roles in the [Disney Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Channel "Disney Channel") series _[Bizaardvark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bizaardvark "Bizaardvark")_ (2016–2019) and the [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") series _[High School Musical: The Musical: The Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_School_Musical:_The_Musical:_The_Series "High School Musical: The Musical: The Series")_ (2019–2022).

Rodrigo shifted her focus to music and signed with [Geffen Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geffen_Records "Geffen Records") in 2020. Her debut studio album, _[Sour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sour_\(album\) "Sour (album)")_ (2021), topped the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") and nine other charts worldwide. It was preceded by the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") number-one singles "[Drivers License](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drivers_License_\(song\) "Drivers License (song)")" and "[Good 4 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_4_U "Good 4 U")". She was the subject of a documentary, _[Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Rodrigo:_Driving_Home_2_U "Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U")_ (2022). Her next two studio albums, _[Guts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guts_\(album\) "Guts (album)")_ (2023) and _[You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Seem_Pretty_Sad_for_a_Girl_So_in_Love "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love")_ (2026), produced the US number-one singles "[Vampire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vampire_\(Olivia_Rodrigo_song\) "Vampire (Olivia Rodrigo song)")" and "[Drop Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drop_Dead "Drop Dead")" respectively, making her the first artist to have each lead single from their first three albums debut atop the chart.

[Rodrigo's accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Olivia_Rodrigo "List of awards and nominations received by Olivia Rodrigo") include three [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"), four [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards"), and seven [_Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Awards "Billboard Music Awards"). She was named _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time (magazine)")_'s [Entertainer of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Entertainer_of_the_Year "Time Entertainer of the Year") in 2021, _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s [Woman of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Woman_of_the_Year "Billboard Woman of the Year") in 2022, and [ASCAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCAP "ASCAP")'s Pop Music Songwriter of the Year in both 2022 and 2024.

## Early life

Olivia Isabel Rodrigo[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) was born on February 20, 2003,[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) at the [Rancho Springs Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancho_Springs_Medical_Center "Rancho Springs Medical Center") in [Murrieta, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murrieta,_California "Murrieta, California"), to Jennifer ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Née "Née") Lee), a schoolteacher, and Chris, a [family therapist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_therapist "Family therapist").[\[3\]](#cite_note-born_info_1-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) She is an only child,[\[5\]](#cite_note-snapes-heartbreak-5) and grew up in neighboring [Temecula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temecula "Temecula").[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) Rodrigo was born half-deaf in her left ear.[\[7\]](#cite_note-RS-7) She is half-Filipina and identifies as [Filipino American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipino_American "Filipino American").[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) Her paternal grandparents and great-grandparents emigrated from the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines"), and her family follows Filipino traditions, including preparation of [cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipino_cuisine "Filipino cuisine").[\[10\]](#cite_note-caam-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-BBC-5facts-11) Her mother has German and Irish ancestry.[\[5\]](#cite_note-snapes-heartbreak-5)[\[12\]](#cite_note-abscbn-12) She grew up listening to her parents' favorite [alternative rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_rock "Alternative rock") bands, such as [No Doubt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Doubt "No Doubt"), [Pearl Jam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Jam "Pearl Jam"), [the White Stripes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_White_Stripes "The White Stripes"), and [Green Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Day "Green Day").[\[13\]](#cite_note-variety-musicjourney-13)

Rodrigo attended Lisa J. Mails Elementary School in Murrieta, participating in its after-school musical theater program.[\[14\]](#cite_note-Murrieta2019-14) At age five, her parents signed her up for vocal lessons with Jennifer Dustman, who enrolled Rodrigo in various local singing competitions.[\[15\]](#cite_note-april2021-elle-profile-15) On Dustman's advice, Rodrigo's parents enrolled her in acting lessons.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Geena_Davis_bio-16)[\[17\]](#cite_note-allmusic-bio-17) She began taking piano lessons at age nine.[\[15\]](#cite_note-april2021-elle-profile-15) Rodrigo first became interested in songwriting after listening to [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") songs by [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"),[\[13\]](#cite_note-variety-musicjourney-13) and she was playing guitar by age 12.[\[17\]](#cite_note-allmusic-bio-17) In May 2010, at age seven, she first appeared onscreen in an [Old Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Navy "Old Navy") commercial.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

## Career

### 2015–2019: Career beginnings and acting

In 2015, at age twelve, Rodrigo made her acting debut, in the lead role of [Grace Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace_Thomas "Grace Thomas") in the direct-to-video film _[An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An_American_Girl:_Grace_Stirs_Up_Success "An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success")_.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) She attended Dorothy McElhinney Middle School in Murrieta for a year, then moved to Los Angeles after landing an acting role in [Disney Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Channel "Disney Channel")'s _[Bizaardvark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bizaardvark "Bizaardvark")_ in 2016;[\[14\]](#cite_note-Murrieta2019-14) she was homeschooled from then until graduating in 2021.[\[5\]](#cite_note-snapes-heartbreak-5)[\[21\]](#cite_note-21) Starring as the character Paige Olvera, a guitarist, she played the role for three seasons.[\[22\]](#cite_note-bizaardvark-22)[\[23\]](#cite_note-23)[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)

In February 2019, she was cast in the starring role of Nini Salazar-Roberts on the [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") series _[High School Musical: The Musical: The Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_School_Musical:_The_Musical:_The_Series "High School Musical: The Musical: The Series")_, which premiered in November of that year.[\[26\]](#cite_note-HSMTS-26) Rodrigo was praised for her performance,[\[27\]](#cite_note-27)[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) with Joel Keller of _[Decider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decider_\(website\) "Decider (website)")_ calling her "especially magnetic".[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) For the series, Rodrigo wrote and performed the promotional single "[All I Want](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_I_Want_\(Olivia_Rodrigo_song\) "All I Want (Olivia Rodrigo song)")", released in November 2019.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) She left the show at the end of its third season to focus on her music career.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

### 2020–2022: _Sour_

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Sour_Tour_2022.jpg/250px-Sour_Tour_2022.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sour_Tour_2022.jpg)

Rodrigo in 2022 during the Sour Tour

Rodrigo signed with [Geffen Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geffen_Records "Geffen Records") in 2020.[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) She negotiated the record deal to secure for herself ownership of the [masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastering_\(audio\) "Mastering (audio)") of her music.[\[5\]](#cite_note-snapes-heartbreak-5) On January 8, 2021, she released her debut single, "[Drivers License](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drivers_License_\(song\) "Drivers License (song)")", which she co-wrote with producer [Dan Nigro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Nigro "Dan Nigro").[\[34\]](#cite_note-34)[\[35\]](#cite_note-thelineofbestfit.com-35) Within the week of its release, "Drivers License" was critically acclaimed,[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) and broke [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify")'s record twice for most daily streams ever for a non-holiday song with over 15.7 million global streams on January 11 and over 17 million global streams the next day.[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) It went on to break another Spotify record for the first song in history to hit 80 million streams in seven days.[\[38\]](#cite_note-38) The song debuted at number one on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"),[\[39\]](#cite_note-DriversLicense_US_Number1-39) and reached number one in numerous other countries.[\[40\]](#cite_note-langford-DLstreaming-40)[\[41\]](#cite_note-shafer-DLstreaming-41) Rodrigo stated in an interview that "It's been the absolute craziest week of my life ... My entire life just, like, shifted in an instant."[\[42\]](#cite_note-42)

On April 1, 2021, Rodrigo released her follow-up single, "[Deja Vu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deja_Vu_\(Olivia_Rodrigo_song\) "Deja Vu (Olivia Rodrigo song)")", which debuted at number eight on the _Billboard_ Hot 100,[\[43\]](#cite_note-trust-2021-43) making her the first artist to debut their first two releases in the top 10 of the Hot 100.[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) The third single preceding her debut album, "[Good 4 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_4_U "Good 4 U")", followed on May 14, 2021, and became her second single to debut at number one on the Hot 100.[\[45\]](#cite_note-45)[\[46\]](#cite_note-46) _[Sour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sour_\(album\) "Sour (album)")_, her debut studio album, was released on May 21, 2021, to critical acclaim.[\[47\]](#cite_note-47) _[Slate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slate_\(magazine\) "Slate (magazine)")_'s Chris Molanphy said its first three singles alone established Rodrigo's "early status as [Gen-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gen-Z "Gen-Z")'s most versatile new artist".[\[48\]](#cite_note-molanphy-good4u-48) According to _[Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash_\(magazine\) "Clash (magazine)")_ critic Robin Murray, Rodrigo is regarded as one of Generation Z's finest artists,[\[49\]](#cite_note-49) while _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")_ dubbed her "the voice of her generation" in its cover story of Rodrigo.[\[13\]](#cite_note-variety-musicjourney-13) _Sour_ debuted at number one on the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") chart and spent a total of five weeks at the spot, becoming the longest reigning number-one album by a female artist in 2021.[\[50\]](#cite_note-50)

In June 2021, Rodrigo premiered _Sour Prom_, a [prom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prom "Prom")\-themed concert film on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[\[51\]](#cite_note-51) Three days later, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time (magazine)")_ named her Entertainer of the Year.[\[52\]](#cite_note-time-52) In an Instagram post on December 24, 2021, Rodrigo uploaded a snippet of a Christmas song called "The Bels" that she wrote and recorded at age five.[\[53\]](#cite_note-53)[\[54\]](#cite_note-54) According to _Billboard_, Rodrigo closed 2021 as the bestselling singles artist worldwide,[\[55\]](#cite_note-55) while placing eight songs on the year-end [Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") chart, including "Drivers License" at number four, "Good 4 U" at number nine, and "Deja Vu" at number 27.[\[56\]](#cite_note-56) In the US and UK, _Sour_ was respectively the third and fourth bestselling album of 2021.[\[57\]](#cite_note-forbes-bestselling-57)[\[58\]](#cite_note-OCC-bestselling-58) _Sour_ and "Drivers License" were also respectively Spotify's most-streamed album and song globally.[\[59\]](#cite_note-spotify2021-59) The [International Federation of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry") (IFPI) ranked Rodrigo as the tenth bestselling artist of 2021 and _Sour_ as the second bestselling album of 2021.[\[60\]](#cite_note-60)

To support _Sour_, Rodrigo embarked on her debut headlining tour, the [Sour Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sour_Tour "Sour Tour"), which ran from April to July 2022; it included stops in the United States, Canada, and Europe.[\[61\]](#cite_note-61) In February 2022, Rodrigo signed with [Lighthouse Management + Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse_Management_+_Media "Lighthouse Management + Media"), entering into a management arrangement with [Aleen Keshishian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleen_Keshishian "Aleen Keshishian") and Zack Morgenroth.[\[62\]](#cite_note-62) Rodrigo's Disney+ documentary film _[Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Rodrigo:_Driving_Home_2_U "Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U")_, which details the making of _Sour_, was released on March 25, 2022.[\[63\]](#cite_note-pitchfork-63) Rodrigo received seven nominations at the [64th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/64th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "64th Annual Grammy Awards"), including [Best New Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist"), [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") and [Best Pop Vocal Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Pop_Vocal_Album "Best Pop Vocal Album") for _Sour_, and [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year"), [Best Pop Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Pop_Solo_Performance "Best Pop Solo Performance") and [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year") for "Drivers License".[\[64\]](#cite_note-64) She won the awards for Best New Artist, Best Pop Vocal Album for _Sour_, and Best Pop Solo Performance for "Drivers License".[\[65\]](#cite_note-Grammys_2022-65) In 2022, while crafting her next album, _[Guts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guts_\(album\) "Guts (album)")_, Rodrigo attended a poetry class at [University of Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California "University of Southern California"), and ended up repurposing one of her homework pieces into the song "[Lacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacy_\(song\) "Lacy (song)")", which would appear on the album's tracklist.[\[66\]](#cite_note-66)

### 2023–2025: _Guts_

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Olivia_Rodrigo_%40_Theatre_at_Ace_Hotel_10_09_2023_%2853423846745%29.jpg/250px-Olivia_Rodrigo_%40_Theatre_at_Ace_Hotel_10_09_2023_%2853423846745%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Olivia_Rodrigo_@_Theatre_at_Ace_Hotel_10_09_2023_\(53423846745\).jpg)

Rodrigo performing at the [Theatre at Ace Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatre_at_Ace_Hotel "Theatre at Ace Hotel") in 2023

On August 16, 2023, Rodrigo became the youngest artist to receive the [Brit Billion Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Billion_Award "Brit Billion Award") for achieving over one billion digital streams in the United Kingdom. She was the 19th artist to receive a BRIT Billion Award.[\[67\]](#cite_note-67) Rodrigo's second album, _Guts_, was released on September 8, 2023, and debuted atop the _Billboard_ 200. She stated that the album was about "growing pains" and self-discovery. Going into the album cycle, she felt that she had grown "10 years" between the ages of 18 and 20.[\[68\]](#cite_note-68) _Guts_ received critical acclaim from various outlets and was later declared by BBC News as the most critically acclaimed album of 2023.[\[69\]](#cite_note-69) The album's lead single, "[Vampire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vampire_\(Olivia_Rodrigo_song\) "Vampire (Olivia Rodrigo song)")", was released on June 30. It became Rodrigo's third single to [debut atop the _Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_number_ones_of_2023 "List of Billboard Hot 100 number ones of 2023"), making her the first artist ever to debut the lead singles from two career-opening albums at No. 1 on the Hot 100.[\[70\]](#cite_note-70)[\[71\]](#cite_note-71)[\[72\]](#cite_note-72) The album's second single, "[Bad Idea Right?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Idea_Right%3F "Bad Idea Right?")", was released on August 11, 2023,[\[73\]](#cite_note-73) and reached the top 10 in the US and UK.[\[74\]](#cite_note-74)[\[75\]](#cite_note-75)

On October 9, 2023, Rodrigo performed songs from _Guts_ in an exclusive concert in partnership with American Express at [Los Angeles Theater at Ace Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ace_Hotel_Los_Angeles "Ace Hotel Los Angeles"). All proceeds from ticket sales went to her Fund 4 Good nonprofit organization.[\[76\]](#cite_note-76) On October 18, 2023, Rodrigo announced that the four secret tracks released on limited vinyl editions of _Guts_ would be released as a limited vinyl-exclusive EP to commemorate [Record Store Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_Store_Day "Record Store Day") (RSD) Black Friday.[\[77\]](#cite_note-77) The EP _Guts: The Secret Tracks_ ranked as one of the top sellers during Record Store Day.[\[78\]](#cite_note-78) On November 3, Rodrigo released the song "[Can't Catch Me Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Catch_Me_Now "Can't Catch Me Now")" for _[The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hunger_Games:_The_Ballad_of_Songbirds_&_Snakes "The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes")_.[\[79\]](#cite_note-79) The song won the [Hollywood Music in Media Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Music_in_Media_Award "Hollywood Music in Media Award") for [Best Original Song in a Sci-Fi, Fantasy or Horror Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Music_in_Media_Award_for_Best_Original_Song_in_a_Sci-Fi,_Fantasy_or_Horror_Film "Hollywood Music in Media Award for Best Original Song in a Sci-Fi, Fantasy or Horror Film") at the [2023 ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/14th_Hollywood_Music_in_Media_Awards "14th Hollywood Music in Media Awards").[\[80\]](#cite_note-80)

To support _Guts_, Rodrigo embarked on her second headlining tour, the [Guts World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guts_World_Tour "Guts World Tour"), from February 2024 to July 2025, visiting North America, Europe, Asia, and Oceania.[\[81\]](#cite_note-81)[\[82\]](#cite_note-82) On March 22, 2024, Rodrigo released a deluxe version of _Guts_, titled _Guts (Spilled)_, with five additional songs, including the four secret tracks from the vinyl variants.[\[83\]](#cite_note-83) On April 13, 2024, Rodrigo made a special guest appearance at [No Doubt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Doubt "No Doubt")'s [Coachella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella "Coachella") show, where she performed the band's 2000 single "[Bathwater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bathwater_\(song\) "Bathwater (song)")" alongside them.[\[84\]](#cite_note-84) On October 2, 2024, Rodrigo announced the _[Guts World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guts_World_Tour "Guts World Tour")_ concert film, which was released on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") on October 29.[\[85\]](#cite_note-85)

Rodrigo performed at several music festivals in June 2025. On June 7, she headlined the second day of the [Governors Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Ball "Governors Ball"), where she performed a cover of "[Burning Down the House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_Down_the_House "Burning Down the House")" with musician [David Byrne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Byrne "David Byrne"), founding member of [Talking Heads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talking_Heads "Talking Heads").[\[86\]](#cite_note-86)[\[87\]](#cite_note-87)[\[88\]](#cite_note-88) She was the headlining act for the 2025 BST Hyde Park Show on June 27, with support from [The Last Dinner Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_Dinner_Party "The Last Dinner Party") and [Girl in Red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girl_in_Red "Girl in Red").[\[89\]](#cite_note-89) Two days later, on June 29, she headlined the final day of the [2025 Glastonbury Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Glastonbury_Festival "2025 Glastonbury Festival") and performed on the [Pyramid Stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyramid_Stage "Pyramid Stage") in her largest performance in the UK to date. Her concert included a guest appearance by [Robert Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Smith_\(musician\) "Robert Smith (musician)"), with whom Rodrigo sang two songs by [the Cure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cure "The Cure"), "[Just like Heaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_like_Heaven_\(The_Cure_song\) "Just like Heaven (The Cure song)")" and "[Friday I'm in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friday_I'm_in_Love "Friday I'm in Love")".[\[90\]](#cite_note-90)[\[91\]](#cite_note-91) On August 1, she headlined the second day of [Lollapalooza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lollapalooza "Lollapalooza") Chicago 2025, with [Weezer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weezer "Weezer") guesting to perform the songs "[Buddy Holly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_Holly_\(song\) "Buddy Holly (song)")" and "[Say It Ain't So](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Say_It_Ain't_So "Say It Ain't So")" with her.[\[92\]](#cite_note-92) Rodrigo was featured in the documentary film _[Lilith Fair: Building a Mystery – The Untold Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lilith_Fair:_Building_a_Mystery "Lilith Fair: Building a Mystery")_ (2025), reflecting on the legacy of the all-female music festival.[\[93\]](#cite_note-93) On November 9, Rodrigo teamed up with [Feist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feist_\(singer\) "Feist (singer)") to perform a rendition of "[We're Going to Be Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We're_Going_to_Be_Friends "We're Going to Be Friends")" by [the White Stripes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_White_Stripes "The White Stripes") at the band's [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") induction ceremony.[\[94\]](#cite_note-94)

### 2026–present: _You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love_

On April 2, 2026, Rodrigo announced her third studio album, _[You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Seem_Pretty_Sad_for_a_Girl_So_in_Love "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love")_.[\[95\]](#cite_note-USAT-2026-95) Its lead single, "[Drop Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drop_Dead "Drop Dead")", was released on April 17[\[96\]](#cite_note-96) and debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, extending her record as the first artist to debut the lead singles from their first three albums at the summit.[\[97\]](#cite_note-97) "[The Cure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cure_\(Olivia_Rodrigo_song\) "The Cure (Olivia Rodrigo song)")" was released on May 22 as the album's second single,[\[98\]](#cite_note-98) followed by "[Stupid Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stupid_Song "Stupid Song")" as its third single alongside its release, accompanied by a music video.[\[99\]](#cite_note-99) Released on June 12, _You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love_ debuted at number one on the US _Billboard_ 200 and the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart"), marking Rodrigo's largest first-week sales in both countries.[\[100\]](#cite_note-yspsus-100)[\[101\]](#cite_note-yspsuk-101) Her third-consecutive US number-one album, it made her the first artist to have their first three lead singles and studio albums debut atop the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and _Billboard_ 200.[\[100\]](#cite_note-yspsus-100) In the UK, she became the youngest international artist to earn more than 100,000 opening-week units since [Britney Spears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_Spears "Britney Spears") in 2004.[\[101\]](#cite_note-yspsuk-101)

On April 18, Rodrigo appeared as a surprise guest on [Addison Rae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addison_Rae "Addison Rae")'s set at [Coachella 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_2026 "Coachella 2026") and debuted "Drop Dead" live.[\[102\]](#cite_note-102) On April 30, Rodrigo announced her third concert tour, [the Unraveled Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Unraveled_Tour "The Unraveled Tour"), in support of _You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love_. Consisting of 86 dates across North America and Europe, the tour will begin on September 25, 2026, in [Hartford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hartford "Hartford"), and conclude on May 10, 2027, in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"). Supporting acts include [Devon Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devon_Again "Devon Again"), [Die Spitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die_Spitz "Die Spitz"), [Grace Ives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace_Ives "Grace Ives"), [The Last Dinner Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_Dinner_Party "The Last Dinner Party") and [Wolf Alice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolf_Alice "Wolf Alice").[\[103\]](#cite_note-103)[\[104\]](#cite_note-104) Rodrigo appeared as both host and musical guest on _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")_ on May 2;[\[105\]](#cite_note-SNL2026-105) she performed "Drop Dead" and debuted another track, "[Begged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Begged_\(song\) "Begged (song)")".[\[106\]](#cite_note-106) During her surprise set at [Primavera Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primavera_Sound "Primavera Sound") on June 6, she debuted her new track, "[What's Wrong with Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What's_Wrong_with_Me "What's Wrong with Me")" with Robert Smith of the Cure.[\[107\]](#cite_note-107) On June 22, Rodrigo announced [Daisy Chain Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daisy_Chain_Fields "Daisy Chain Fields"), an all-female music festival set to take place on August 29 in [Irvine, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irvine,_California "Irvine, California"), with 16 other female artists set to perform and all net proceeds dire
